Cancer Cachexia
Cancer Cachexia Syndrome (CCS) refers to the characteristic wasting seen in 50–80% 
of cancer patients with advanced disease and is most prevalent among patients with 
GI and lung cancers.73,74 With the exception of breast cancer, patients with solid 
tumors are at greater risk of developing CCS.75 Features of cancer cachexia include 
weight loss, anorexia, fatigue, early satiety, depression, reduced quality of life, and 
asthenia.64,76 CCS is a complex metabolic state which leads to depletion of energy and 
muscle stores.
